class.name: NNPointGrid3DSearchSpace
class.brief_description: Creates and uses a [Node3D] point grid to define the search space.
class.description: Creates and uses a [Node3D] point grid to define the search space. Set [member point_grid_parent_node] to the [Node3D] under which the generated point nodes will be added. The points are created relative to the parent node's position and inherit its transform, with the parent node at the center of the grid. Points are generated in pairs: a base point and a lattice point. For example, in a flat square grid on the XZ plane, a base point might be placed every 2 units on X and 1 unit on Z. This step between base points is controlled by [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector], which also controls grid density: smaller spacing produces more points to fill the volume defined by [member grid_size]. The lattice point is placed at [member point_grid_lattice_vector] relative to each base point. For the square grid above, setting [member point_grid_lattice_vector] to [code]Vector3(1, 0, 0)[/code] places the lattice point 1 unit along +X from each base point. During grid generation, the X, Y, and Z axes are stepped from [code]-0.5 * grid_size[/code] to [code]0.5 * grid_size[/code] in increments of [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector] (with the default [code]grid_size.y == 0[/code], a single horizontal layer at [code]y = 0[/code] is generated). At each step, both the base point and [code]base_point + point_grid_lattice_vector[/code] are added. Shifting the lattice point (for example, to [code]Vector3(1, 0, 0.5)[/code]) produces staggered or triangular layouts. [b]Warning:[/b] When creating point grids, it is very easy to generate a large number of points for a search space. When [member use_navigation_mesh_positions] is [code]true[/code] and [member navigation_map_rid] is valid (initialized automatically from the viewport's 3D world navigation map), each point's global position is snapped during query preprocessing to the closest point on that navigation map using [method NavigationServer3D.map_get_closest_point]. To give generated points a visible debug representation or custom script, add a [Node3D] (or derived node, such as [MeshInstance3D]) named [code]DEBUG[/code] as a direct child of this [NNPointGrid3DSearchSpace]. Grid generation duplicates that [code]DEBUG[/code] child for every generated point instead of creating plain [Node3D] nodes. Before duplicating the template node, grid creation calls [method Object.set] for [code]score[/code] ([code]0.0[/code]) and [code]is_filtered[/code] ([code]false[/code]). If your [code]DEBUG[/code] node's script defines those properties and [member NNNQSSearchSpaces.is_run_in_debug_mode] is enabled, they are updated on each point node as criteria evaluate it.

members.member: The grid width, height, and depth, centered on [member point_grid_parent_node].

The [NavigationServer3D] map [RID] used when [member use_navigation_mesh_positions] is [code]true[/code]. Populated automatically from the viewport's 3D world navigation map when the search space initializes.
Offset added to the local position of every point in the grid. With [member use_navigation_mesh_positions], the offset point is the one snapped to the navigation map.
The grid of points as [Node3D] nodes.

The step size along the X, Y, and Z axes between consecutive base points. All three components must be finite and greater than [code]0[/code]; invalid values are ignored and keep the previous spacing.

Selects a lattice preset that overwrites [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector] and [member point_grid_lattice_vector]. Values are: [code]Square:0[/code] (spacing [code](2, 1, 1)[/code], lattice [code](1, 0, 0)[/code]), [code]Triangular:1[/code] (spacing [code](1, 1, 2)[/code], lattice [code](-0.5, 0, 1)[/code]), [code]CenteredRectangular:2[/code] (spacing [code](2, 1, 1)[/code], lattice [code](1, 0, 0.5)[/code]), [code]Rectangular:3[/code] (spacing [code](2, 1, 0.5)[/code], lattice [code](1, 0, 0)[/code]), and [code]Custom:4[/code] (leaves the spacing and lattice vectors unchanged).
Local offset from each base point where its paired lattice point is placed. Together with [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector], this defines the repeating pattern of the grid.
The node the generated point nodes are added to. The grid is positioned relative to this node, so moving it moves the grid. No grid is created when this is not set.
The overall shape of the generated grid. Only [code]Rectangle:0[/code] is implemented, which fills the box region defined by [member grid_size].

If [code]true[/code] and [member navigation_map_rid] is valid, each point's global position is snapped to the closest point on the navigation map via [method NavigationServer3D.map_get_closest_point] during query preprocessing.
